observations: The practiced skill’s definition and the explicitly competent performance sense supply the affix base.
Latter-member elision gives a different history for mārdaṅgika. The objection names a mere maker.
Paiṭharika occurs on the restricted craft example list. The lexicon derives it from piṭhara and qualifies the real-world gloss.
The expanded transcription gives maurajika with an independently named muraja base. The Kielhorn-locus transcription lacks that example.
Maḍḍuka and jharjhara each have two printed alternatives in the one performance sense.
The four cited bases carry the praharaṇa relation at the given headwords.
Dhanus has affix ka and a separate ṣ replacing internal visarga.
Paraśvadha has both suffixes with the segmental pattern shared and the two accents ordered by marker.
The received rule and the cited ordinary outcomes have long ī.
The Bhāṣya tests kak and then ikak and distinguishes redundant from causally effective pronounced i.
Nyāsa also considers the role of avagraha and the threat from base-final deletion.
The verse in both selected displays contains short śāktika as an inner member.
Jayamaṅgalā p. 84 prints short yāṣṭika in the paraphrase and expressly names yaṣṭi while citing the long īkak rule.
The aggregation is treated as a collective of named members in the explanatory account.
Bhaṭṭi 5.78 attests pāraśvadhika on the left of rāma.
Māgha 2.27 gives a free genitive singular dhānuṣkasya.
decisions: Admit the named practiced performances. Instrument making alone fails in the cited mṛdaṅga construction.
Retain both latter-member elision and licensed metonymy for mārdaṅgika at one segmental case query.
Allow muraja → maurajika in the attested expanded transcription and lexicon, with critical print alignment Open.
Allow the named paiṭharika case fibre. Exact activity stays Open.
Keep both accepted suffixes for each of the two named forms. Cases run on both stems within each sense.
Fix the us-conditioned k affix and the internal ṣ contact as different events.
Preserve ṭhañ and ṭhak under ca for paraśvadha. The mention of paraśu as a separate lexical item gives no extension of the named exception.
Use the received long-suffix route for the two selected free paradigms.
Retain kak and ikak as dialogue proposals, with the 6.1.101 identity stated separately from the numeric link on the transcription.
Admit both short spellings only at their exact textual compound addresses. One passage uses śakti and the other yaṣṭi.
Keep the aggregate inside the dual adjective. It provides no standalone short predicate or case grid.
Under the 5.78 epithet construction, right-hand rāma owns the visible genitive.
Attach the actual dhānuṣkasya token to precisely the existing written free GENsg coordinate of this stage.
